text:
Maya: Heads up — we started seeing a p99 spike on 8xA100 after the kernel-selector change from PR #4123. Profiling points to repeated all-reduce stalls around layers 22-26.

Trey: Seen that on my local repro too. The PR only touched kernel dispatch heuristics, but that can change tensor shapes going into comms.

Maya: I ran a few quick traces and nvprof snippets. When the model hits those layers we get bursts of very small tensors which seem to serialize all-reduce. Also KV-cache prefetch creates extra tiny messages.

Anika: Are we using per-op channels or the default single channel? And what are the NCCL envs right now?

Maya: Current env on the canary runs: 
```bash
NCCL_ALGO=ring
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP
NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=4
```
Kernel selector: fused-attn-v2 for seq <= 1024 else fallback to generic. That fallback creates a different kernel size distribution.

Trey: Can you paste the flamegraph lines for the hot path?

Maya: Key stack (condensed): 
"ncclAllReduce -> wait_event -> cudaLaunchKernel(attn_fwd) -> stall
... -> kvcache_prefetch_rpc -> small-send"
So two patterns: (1) All-reduce stalls when many small tensors hit the ring, (2) KV prefetch bursts interleave and amplify contention.

Luke: Hypothesis: LL128 helps for medium-large tensors but for many tiny tensors it adds proto overhead. Try Simple proto for small messages and LL128 for larger ones — but NCCL can't do per-op proto, so maybe increase parallelism (#rings) or change channel mapping. Also check NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME so we don't leak on the wrong NIC.

Anika: Agreed. Also check NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE and NCCL_MAX_NRINGS — More rings can help overlap multiple small reductions.

perfbot: perf CI summary for the quick experiment suite:
- ring / LL128 / 4rings -> p99: 210ms
- ring / Simple / 8rings -> p99: 160ms (tail improved, median slightly up)
- tree / LL / 6rings -> p99: 170ms
Artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/1945067890/

Trey: That looks promising. Plan: run a 12-hour soak on canary with ring/Simple/8rings + bump kvcache prefetch batch size (reduce RPC count, aggregate to ~16KB) and change kernel selector to prefer queued-matmul for matmul sizes < 512.

Maya: I'll produce a feature-flagged build with those envs and the kvcache batching change and kick off the soak. Pushing canary in ~30m and will share traces.

Anika: Add a regression alert hook (perf-regression-bot) and wire up the eval prompt set so we can detect quality drift if kernel change affects outputs.

Luke: I'll update the internal comm tuning doc with the experiment matrix and results, and add the nccl-tests microbench script used for skewed-size workloads.

Maya: Sounds good. If soak looks stable we'll roll to dedicated pools tomorrow morning. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Trey: +1
